admission.reason: Use the fixed mod-8 phase structure and bounded second difference of the order-one quotient to replace repeated full-size division by exact quotient/remainder state transport plus a fixed normalized reciprocal correction table.

methods.name: BRC phase quotient/remainder transport
capabilities: exact five-phase transport of divmod(2*h*J,4*m+h) on the common order-one deep tail
two direct seed divmods per mod-8 source phase followed by recurrence-only quotient generation
proved phase second-difference bounds -3..51 for h=1 and -3..99 for h=2
exact product-free residual recurrence using retained roots, quotients and division remainders
512-entry 10-bit normalized lower reciprocal table with 1024-byte logical raw payload
proved non-negative correction estimate within at most one plus one exact comparison
optional large-integer backend that composes with the order-one linear BRC tail and staged square-gap cascade
methods.core_law: For one fixed mod-8 phase, S_h(m)=2h*sqrt(mN)/(4m+h) has 0<=Delta_8^2 S_h<=48h on 4m^5>=N. Since q_h=floor(2h*floor(sqrt(mN))/(4m+h)) differs from S_h by less than 2, its exact integer second difference is in [-3,51] for h=1 and [-3,99] for h=2. With X_i=q_i D_i+r_i and D_(i+1)=D_i+32, the residual relative to qhat=2q_i-q_(i-1) is rho=2h(J_(i+1)-2J_i+J_(i-1))+2r_i-r_(i-1)+64(q_(i-1)-q_i), so the next quotient/remainder follows from only a bounded correction. A 10-bit upper-bucket reciprocal seed estimates each non-negative correction from below within one.
methods.hard_boundary: Exact only on the already-certified common order-one deep tail and increasing odd-N mod-8 representative stream. Native big-integer division remains faster in the measured 1024/2048-bit Python cohorts; the tracker is an optional large-integer long-stream backend with a runtime-dependent crossover. It does not reduce the multiplier horizon, alter factorization complexity, or imply RSA practicality.
